rules.R1_parentOfLastResort: An item is re-parented to its category only if its current parent is an epic, the Initiative root (#1511 itself), or the retired Hardening epic #1511 (its 8 features, under D1 v2). An item with a meaningful parent (a program tracker, a T1 feature, a Hardening feature, a 2026 scaffold story, the item its bug regresses) keeps it and carries the Category field.
rules.R2_assignment: File by the code whose behaviour changes, not the surface that breaks. Evidence, in order: the merged diff (src and shared/ lines; tests, docs and harnesses excluded) for merged work; the fix sites or remaining scope the body states for open work; the subject the title names when neither exists. R2 picks the project; when one project hosts several categories (Database.Storage: Core C01/C02/C03; Database.Sql: SQL C01..C08), the category definitions decide. A batch commit that closed many scaffold tasks at once is not evidence for any one of them.
rules.R2_tieBreak1: When two components change about equally, the category first in .rules.precedence wins (deepest layer first; kernel before every model). About equally is checked against the merged diff: no other category may hold 2x or more of the chosen category's src lines, and tie-break 2's no-dominant-model premise is checked the same way (build.js; a flagged row is re-derived or carries the tally that overrides the file classifier).
rules.R2_tieBreak2: An item that changes two or more models with no dominant model goes to the kernel category its shared concern names (20 items: #1005, #1015, #1087, #1091, #1101, #1102, #1104, #1160, #1219, #1225, #1247, #1271, #1275, #1287, #1356, #1362, #1364, #1372, #1391, #1538). Cost accepted: Core counts include model code that implements a shared rule in several models.
rules.R2_tieBreak3: Only then, the component named first in the title.
rules.R3_bugs: A bug is a child of the item whose acceptance it violates, open or closed, without reopening it; otherwise it files under its category (bug-policy.md).
rules.R4_categoriesNeverClose: A category is a container for the life of the area.
rules.R5_scaffoldDivergence: Withdrawn in v2 (realign-v2/hardening.md section 4). Every scaffold descendant keeps its scaffold parent and takes its category by field only, as R1 already does for program and T1 children: 21 of v1's 25 R5 moves took a child whose body names that parent as its source of truth, the rest are named by the parent's Scope bullets, and 6 open parents would have read complete while their own scope sat in Core. The ten scaffold features themselves are still re-parented to their categories by R1.
rules.R6_concernCategories: Core C14 (observability: owns every EventSource, counter and the runtime diagnostic-code catalogue), C15 (API shape and conventions: owns no code) and C18 (testing and quality gates: owns Database.Testing, shared test infrastructure, cross-engine conformance, probes and CI/benchmark gates) beat R2 only when the concern itself is the deliverable and no product behaviour changes. Tests of one component file with that component; a probe that lands a fix files by the fix; tracing added to one component files in C14 because the EventSource is C14 code. C16 is not a concern category: it is R2 tie-break 2's home for multi-model bulk work.
rules.R7_containers: An item whose deliverable is its sub-issues takes the plurality category of its direct children (closed-not-delivered children excluded); a tie is broken by the subject its title names first, then by precedence. When its children cross two or more epics, the subject its title (its charter) names decides (#1353 -> C13, #1517 -> C07, #1519 -> C16, #49, #56, #63 -> their model service categories). A container with remaining scope of its own is filed by R2 on that scope (#862). The Hardening gate #1511 (D1 v2) is the one item in L03.02.09.C01 that tracks a program.
rules.coreMembership: #31's criterion is that shared engine work is represented separately from the model features. An item files in Core when (a) its change lands mainly in kernel code (R2: the dominant project of the merged diff, else the body's fix sites or remaining scope), (b) it changes two or more models with no dominant model (tie-break 2: one shared rule implemented per model), (c) kernel and model code change about equally (tie-break 1, kernel first), (d) a Core concern is the deliverable and no product behaviour changes (R6), or (e) a stated boundary gives the subject no model home (replication, C17: #1257 deleted every model satellite). A change that lands mainly in one model's code is that model's, never Core. Of the 386 items, 18 filed under a model epic today enter Core on these terms.
rules.withinModelEngines: In SQL, Documents and Graph the language category owns coverage (which constructs are accepted and what they mean, including the operator a new construct needs); the planning/execution category owns how an accepted construct runs (plan choice, access paths, algorithms, memory and work bounds). In SQL only, types, literals, casts, operators, the bound expression tree and functions are L03.02.02.C08.
